slot.brief: Compare two given complexes differing only in ligand field strength; predict high-spin vs low-spin and number of unpaired electrons.

stem: Consider the complexes $\text{[CoF}_6\text{]}^{3-}$ and $\text{[Co(NH}_3\text{)}_6\text{]}^{3+}$. The spin states and the number of unpaired electrons in these complexes are, respectively:

verdicts.working: Both complexes contain Co(III), which is d⁶. In octahedral [CoF₆]³⁻, weak-field F⁻ gives high-spin d⁶ with 4 unpaired electrons; in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, Co(III) with NH₃ is low-spin, t₂g⁶, with 0 unpaired electrons.

working:
Co³⁺ (d⁶). F⁻ is a weak field ligand → small Δ → high‑spin t₂g⁴ e_g² → 4 unpaired electrons.
NH₃ is a strong field ligand → large Δ → low‑spin t₂g⁶ e_g⁰ → 0 unpaired electrons.
Thus [CoF₆]³⁻ is high‑spin with 4 unpaired; [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is low‑spin with 0 unpaired.

Independent check: Both complexes contain Co(III), which is d⁶. In octahedral [CoF₆]³⁻, weak-field F⁻ gives high-spin d⁶ with 4 unpaired electrons; in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, Co(III) with NH₃ is low-spin, t₂g⁶, with 0 unpaired electrons.
solution:
Both complexes contain Co$^{3+}$ ($d^6$) in an octahedral field. F$^-$ is a weak-field ligand, so $[\mathrm{CoF_6}]^{3-}$ is high-spin: $t_{2g}^4e_g^2$, with 4 unpaired electrons.
NH$_3$ gives a low-spin complex: $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{3+}$ has $t_{2g}^6e_g^0$, with 0 unpaired electrons.
